ops.title: Go's -run/-skip are unanchored: anchor them before trusting a test measurement
ops.body:
Go's `-run` and `-skip` are UNANCHORED regexes, per `/`-separated element. A pattern naming a test whose name is a *prefix* of another test silently measures both.

`-run 'TestShipGateProbe'` also matches `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes`. Because that sibling has no subtests, a trailing `/subtest` element does not filter it out — it runs in full whatever subtest you asked for:

| invocation | result |
|---|---|
| `-run 'TestShipGateProbe'` | 23.9s — `TestShipGateProbe (2.13s)` + `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes (20.23s)` |
| `-run '^TestShipGateProbe$'` | 3.7s |
| `-run '^TestShipGateProbe$/^reachable$'` | 2.0s |

This cost two separate wrong conclusions on the same bug (18c5344):

1. `-run 'TestShipGateProbe/<subtest>'` made every single subtest look like it took ~21s, which read as a fixed ~20s package-setup cost. There is no such cost — package overhead is ~1.5s (binary start + race init). It was the sibling paying `gtProbeTimeout` on every invocation.
2. The bug's own workaround, `-skip 'TestShipGateProbe'`, silently skipped the genuine 20.35s `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes`, understating the package total by ~23s.

**Anchor with `^...$` on every element** whenever a timing or a pass/fail conclusion depends on exactly which tests ran. `internal/cli` is especially exposed: it has several prefix-sharing pairs (`TestShipGateProbe`/`TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes`, `TestShipJJHunkScopedLive`/`TestShipJJHunkScopedSubdirLive`).

The failure mode is silent in both directions — a too-slow number from an extra test, or a too-fast one from a skipped test — and nothing in the output says which tests the filter actually selected. `-v` does, which is the cheap check when a number looks wrong.
